learningObjectives.title: The use of scripture in worship and life

questions.q: What is the Christian belief that God is three persons in one being called?
questions.explain: The Trinity is the Christian doctrine that God is one being in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Which three persons make up the Christian Trinity?
questions.explain: Christians believe the one God exists as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.q: The belief that God took human form in the person of Jesus is known as the:
questions.explain: The Incarnation is the belief that God became flesh and lived as a human being in Jesus.

questions.q: A Christian says, 'There is nothing God is unable to do.' Which quality of God is being expressed?
questions.explain: Omnipotent means all-powerful, the belief that God can do anything.

questions.q: Which term describes the Christian belief that God is all-knowing?
questions.explain: Omniscient means all-knowing, the belief that God knows everything.

questions.q: When Christians describe God as omnibenevolent, they mean God is:
questions.explain: Omnibenevolent means all-loving, describing God's perfect goodness towards creation.

questions.q: According to Christian belief, what happened three days after Jesus was crucified?
options: He gave the Sermon on the Mount
questions.explain: The Resurrection is the belief that Jesus rose from the dead, central to Christian faith.

questions.q: Christians describe Jesus as both fully God and fully human. This dual nature is directly linked to the doctrine of the:
questions.explain: The Incarnation holds that in Jesus, God became truly human while remaining fully divine.

questions.q: A believer prays, 'Lord, you see every thought and know all that will happen.' Which attribute of God does this show?
questions.explain: Believing God knows all thoughts and future events expresses His omniscience.

questions.q: The Christian Bible is divided into which two main parts?
options: The Old Testament and the New Testament
questions.explain: The Bible is made up of the Old Testament and the New Testament.

questions.q: What name is given to the first four books of the New Testament, which describe the life of Jesus?
questions.explain: The four Gospels record the life, teaching, death and resurrection of Jesus.

questions.q: The four Gospels of the New Testament are named after:
questions.explain: The four Gospels are Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

questions.q: Christians who believe every word of the Bible is literally and factually true are best described as:
questions.explain: Literalist Christians treat the Bible as the exact, literal word of God to be read as fact.

questions.q: When Christians say the Bible is 'inspired by God', they mean that:
options: Its human writers were guided by God
It was written directly in God's own handwriting
It contains no words written by people
questions.explain: Inspiration means the human authors wrote under the guidance of God, giving the Bible its authority.

questions.q: A Christian argues the Genesis creation account is a symbolic story teaching truths, not a literal scientific report. This approach is best described as:
questions.explain: Liberal Christians may interpret parts of scripture symbolically rather than as literal fact.

questions.q: In many church services the Bible is read aloud to the congregation. This public reading mainly serves to:
options: Teach and guide believers through God's word
questions.explain: Public Bible readings instruct and guide worshippers, giving scripture a central role in worship.

questions.q: A Christian reads the Bible quietly at home each morning to grow in faith. This use of scripture is best described as:
questions.explain: Reading scripture privately for spiritual growth is a form of personal or private devotion.

questions.q: Facing a difficult moral decision, a Christian turns to the Bible for direction. This shows scripture being used as a:
options: Source of moral guidance and authority
questions.explain: Many Christians use the Bible as an authoritative guide for making moral decisions in daily life.

questions.q: The Christian belief that God made the universe out of nothing is expressed by the phrase:
questions.explain: Creation ex nihilo is the belief that God created everything out of nothing.

questions.q: Which part of the Christian Bible shares much of its content with the Jewish scriptures?
questions.explain: The Old Testament contains writings also found in the Jewish scriptures (the Tanakh).

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Religious Studies (0490) syllabus; Christianity: Beliefs & Scriptures
